reference_use.conclusion: Snapshot project d09bc8a / Mathlib 25730c7c plus the pinned simongmt package. No match: Mathlib has no co-area formula (rg 'coarea': no file) and only a fixed-dimension Sard lemma (MeasureTheory/Function/Jacobian.lean), no C¹ Sard-type slice theorem and no countable rectifiability; SimonGMT has no nonlinear co-area formula. Hence the C¹ critical-slice estimate, the C¹ parametric co-area formula and the level-set rectifiability are supplied as children. Available and cited in the children: SimonGMT linear/projection co-area (CoareaLinear.lean, CoareaProjection.lean), Lipschitz and injective area formulas (AreaDomain.lean weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum, injective_area_formula_lipschitzOn, ae_fderivWithin_eq_of_lipschitz_extension, exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional; WeightedArea.lean map_withDensity_areaJacobian_eq and weighted_area_formula_volume_of_injective_derivative for arbitrary integrands), Lipschitz image bound euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, countablyRectifiable_image_contDiffOn_open / _iUnion / _of_measure_zero / CountablyRectifiable.mono, HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique (needs only θ x ≠ 0); Mathlib normDet (normDet_comp, normDet_of_subsingleton, normDet_eq_zero_iff_ker_ne_bot, normDet_sq), μHE[d] = c_d·μH[d] with hausdorffMeasure_le_liminf_sum, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, inverse/implicit function theorem (ContDiffAt.toOpenPartialHomeomorph, OpenPartialHomeomorph.contDiffAt_symm, HasStrictFDerivAt.implicitToOpenPartialHomeomorph), change of variables lintegral_image_eq_lintegral_abs_det_fderiv_mul, Lusin-Souslin MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn / ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding, lintegral_iUnion (arbitrary integrand), lintegral_tsum, lintegral_liminf_le, HasLineDerivAt.unique, Rademacher LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt, WithLp.volume_preserving_toLp. subproblem.title: Hⁿ-null sets have Hᵏ-null slices for Lᵐ-a.e. y (from Eilenberg's inequality)
subproblem.statement: Assume Eilenberg's inequality in exactly the frozen form of the root-level sibling eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality: (E) for all N, m, k ∈ ℕ there is C ∈ ℝ≥0 such that for every A ⊆ ℝ^N, every L ∈ ℝ≥0 and every L-Lipschitz F : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ there is a Borel g : ℝᵐ → [0, ∞] with Hᵏ(A ∩ F⁻¹{y}) ≤ g(y) for every y and ∫ g dLᵐ ≤ C·Lᵐ·H^{m+k}(A). Then for all N, m, k ∈ ℕ, all U, Z ⊆ ℝ^N and every f : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ that is locally Lipschitz on U: if Z ⊆ U and H^{m+k}(Z) = 0, then Hᵏ(Z ∩ f⁻¹{y}) = 0 for Lᵐ-a.e. y ∈ ℝᵐ. Notation (as in the parent): ℝ^d = Rn d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); Hˢ = μHE[s] (applied to an arbitrary set it is the Hausdorff outer measure); Lᵈ = volume; normDet = Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet; P* = LinearMap.adjoint P; DF(u) = fderiv ℝ F u.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (N m k : ℕ), ∃ C : ℝ≥0, ∀ (A : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m) (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith L f → ∃ g : Rn m → ℝ≥0∞, Measurable g ∧ (∀ y, μHE[k] (A ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) ≤ g y) ∧ ∫⁻ y, g y ≤ ((C * L ^ m : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞) * μHE[m + k] A) → ∀ (N m k : ℕ) (U Z : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn m), LocallyLipschitzOn U f → Z ⊆ U → μHE[m + k] Z = 0 → ∀ᵐ y ∂(volume : Measure (Rn m)), μHE[k] (Z ∩ f ⁻¹' {y}) = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part 0.2(i) (null sets have null slices, from Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.9 = the sibling eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality, used in the parent for the null parts that Simon passes over at Ch. 3, p. 77, lines 426-428). The hypothesis (E) is exactly that sibling's frozen statement, so the parent discharges it with Submission.eilenberg_upper_integral_inequality. Generalization relative to the parent's 0.2(i): U need not be open (only local Lipschitz continuity on U is used).
1. (Lipschitz pieces.) Fix N, m, k, U, Z, f as in the statement. If U = ∅ then Z = ∅ and there is nothing to prove. For each x ∈ U, local Lipschitz continuity of f on U gives K_x ∈ ℝ≥0 and a set t_x ∈ 𝓝[U] x with f K_x-Lipschitz on t_x; by the definition of 𝓝[U] x choose an open O_x ∋ x with O_x ∩ U ⊆ t_x. Thus f is K_x-Lipschitz on O_x ∩ U.
2. (Countable subcover.) ℝ^N is second countable, so (Lindelöf, Mathlib isOpen_iUnion_countable) there is a countable T ⊆ U with ⋃_{x∈T} O_x = ⋃_{x∈U} O_x ⊇ U.
3. (Global extensions.) For x ∈ T extend f|_{O_x ∩ U} to a globally Lipschitz map f_x : ℝ^N → ℝᵐ with some constant L_x, f_x = f on O_x ∩ U (coordinatewise McShane extension, Simon Ch. 2, 1.2; in Lean SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_lipschitz_extension_finiteDimensional, or Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi composed with the linear equivalence ℝᵐ ≅ (Fin m → ℝ)).
4. (Eilenberg.) Let C be the constant given by (E) for (N, m, k). For x ∈ T apply (E) with A := Z ∩ O_x, F := f_x, L := L_x: there is a Borel g_x : ℝᵐ → [0, ∞] with Hᵏ(Z ∩ O_x ∩ f_x⁻¹{y}) ≤ g_x(y) for all y and ∫ g_x dLᵐ ≤ C·L_xᵐ·H^{m+k}(Z ∩ O_x) ≤ C·L_xᵐ·H^{m+k}(Z) = 0 (monotonicity of the outer measure). As g_x is measurable with ∫ g_x = 0, g_x = 0 Lᵐ-a.e. (lintegral_eq_zero_iff).
5. (The extension does not change the slices.) Since Z ⊆ U and f_x = f on O_x ∩ U, for every y we have Z ∩ O_x ∩ f⁻¹{y} = Z ∩ O_x ∩ f_x⁻¹{y}, hence Hᵏ(Z ∩ O_x ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g_x(y).
6. (Countable union.) Since T is countable, Y := {y : g_x(y) = 0 for all x ∈ T} has full Lᵐ-measure (ae_all_iff). For y ∈ Y, Z ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} O_x gives Z ∩ f⁻¹{y} = ⋃_{x∈T}(Z ∩ O_x ∩ f⁻¹{y}), so by countable subadditivity Hᵏ(Z ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ Σ_{x∈T} g_x(y) = 0. ∎
(Remark, the parent's 0.2(ii): for N = m + k, an Lⁿ-null Z ⊆ ℝⁿ has H^{m+k}(Z) = Lⁿ(Z) = 0 by EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume, so the statement also covers parameter space.)
proof_key_steps: Cover U by countably many relatively open pieces O_x ∩ U on which f is Lipschitz (local Lipschitz property + Lindelöf).
Extend f from each piece to a globally Lipschitz f_x (coordinatewise McShane extension).
Eilenberg (E) for Z ∩ O_x and f_x gives a Borel majorant g_x with ∫ g_x ≤ C·L_xᵐ·H^{m+k}(Z) = 0, so g_x = 0 a.e.
Since f = f_x on O_x ∩ U ⊇ Z ∩ O_x, Hᵏ(Z ∩ O_x ∩ f⁻¹{y}) ≤ g_x(y) = 0 for a.e. y.
Countable subadditivity over the countably many pieces.

audit.reason: Prose and Lean hypotheses match, including arbitrary U. Relative Lipschitz neighborhoods, countable covering, global extensions and Eilenberg majorants give null slices; countable subadditivity completes the exact conclusion without circularity.
